item.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Turkey demand end to Houthi attacks
item.description:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Turkey demand end to Houthi attacks

The R4 group - Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Turkey - has demanded “the immediate and unconditional halt” to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

In a joint statement, the four countries condemned the continuing missile and drone strikes “in the strongest terms”, describing them as a “blatant violation of international law” and Saudi territorial integrity.

They warned that the attacks endanger civilians and threaten the kingdom’s security and stability.

The countries pledged solidarity with Saudi Arabia and held the Houthis “fully accountable”.

item.description:
Saudi authority confirms Houthi attack on Dammam airport

Yemen’s Houthis have struck King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority says.

The authority confirmed the strike shortly after the group announced that it had targeted the airport, the latest Saudi aviation facility to come under Houthi attack.

Officials are assessing the damage at the airport in the kingdom’s Eastern Province. Dammam lies 410km (254 miles) northeast of Riyadh.

item.title: Fresh attack hits Riyadh airport as Houthis warn airlines against using Saudi airspace
item.description:
Fresh attack hits Riyadh airport as Houthis warn airlines against using Saudi airspace

Submitted by MEE staff on Sun, 10/11/2026 - 18:50
A projectile hits a passenger terminal a day after a strike killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300
The scene at Riyadh international airport after strike on Saturday. (Social Media/X)
Off

A fresh attack struck a passenger terminal at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, starting a fire and injuring people a day after a deadly strike on the same airport.

The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said an “unidentified ⁠projectile” hit the terminal. Saudi air defences also intercepted a missile.

Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said the attack “resulted in injuries” but gave no casualty figure.

An “assessment of the damage and verification of the safety of the facilities is ongoing”, the authority added.

Saturday’s attack killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300, making it the deadliest strike on a Gulf country since the US-Israeli war on Iran began on 28 February.

The airport remained closed on Sunday. Saudi civil aviation authorities issued a Notice to Air Missions, or NOTAM, extending the shutdown until 21:00 GMT.

Houthi forces warn against use of Saudi airports following Riyadh attack
Read More »

Such notices alert flight crews to time-sensitive information. Saudi authorities have not separately announced the extension.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree renewed his warning against using Saudi airports and airspace, addressing shipping companies, airlines, employees, workers and travellers.

They are “exposed to targeting and a theatre for operations by our forces”, he wrote on X, while excluding the airports of Mecca and Medina from attacks.

Saree said Houthi forces carried out several operations against King Khalid airport on Saturday, “resulting in the disruption of air traffic at the airport and its complete closure”.

He also listed King Fahd Airport in Dammam, an Aramco-affiliated petrol station and a refinery in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Region among the targets.

Meanwhile, Houthi-run Al Masirah television reported an attack on Sanaa International Airport in Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition has not commented on that report.

item.title: Middle East crisis: Riyadh airport hit again as Houthis claim attacks, including strike that killed 12 – as it happened
item.description:
This live blog is now closed. You can read our latest full report here:

  • Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi authorities say

Some more Gulf reaction to Houthi’s deadly airport attack and continued threats to target Saudi airspace.

In a significant message, the United Arab Emirates has issued a statement in solidarity with Saudi Arabia – expressing support for “all measures aimed at safeguarding the kingdom’s security and stability”.

The UAE message is improtant given the major rupture in relations this year between the two oil-rich kingdoms, first sparked by lingering divisions in Yemen, and made worse by the Iran War and arguments over oil prices which led to the UAE quitting OPEC (currently led by the Saudis) after six decades of membership.

Saturday’s incident comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis ⁠on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this ​week, leaving four people dead and ‌others wounded, and ‌badly damaging an aircraft.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.

item.title: Six Pakistanis wounded and Indian national dies after Riyadh airport attack
item.description:
Six Pakistanis wounded and Indian national dies after Riyadh airport attack

Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif says Saturday’s Houthi strike on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport wounded six Pakistani citizens.

“I pray for their speedy recovery. Our Embassy in Riyadh is in close contact with the Saudi authorities and is extending all possible assistance to the affected families,” he wrote on X.

India’s embassy in Saudi Arabia also confirmed that an Indian citizen had died from wounds suffered in the attack.

Earlier on Sunday, Saudi Arabia’s Civil Aviation Authority reported 12 deaths and 309 injuries.
